title: Tame invariants commute with arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a finite group of order $d$ with $d\in A^\times$, and $M$ an $A$-module with an $A$-linear $G$-action. Write $M^G=\{m:g(m)=m\text{ for every }g\in G\}$. The $A$-linear operator $e_M=d^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}g$ is idempotent, has image $M^G$, and restricts to the identity on $M^G$. For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$, the natural map
$$B\otimes_A M^G\longrightarrow(B\otimes_A M)^G$$
is an isomorphism of $B$-modules, with $G$ acting trivially on $B$. It is natural in equivariant module maps and in $B$. If $M=C$ is a commutative $A$-algebra on which $G$ acts by $A$-algebra automorphisms, this comparison is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras
$$B\otimes_A C^G\simeq(B\otimes_A C)^G.$$
Neither $B$ nor $C$ is required to be flat over $A$. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0H36, remark-when-iso; compare Tag 0BRH, lemma-base-change-invariants. The invertible-order extension to arbitrary scalar rings is the Reynolds idempotent argument.

proof.text: Put $u=d^{-1}\in A$. For $h\in G$, reindexing the finite sum by the permutation $g\mapsto hg$ gives $h(e_M(m))=u\sum_g(hg)(m)=e_M(m)$. If $x\in M^G$, then $e_M(x)=u\sum_gx=udx=x$. Thus $r:M\to M^G$, $r(m)=e_M(m)$, is $A$-linear; with inclusion $j:M^G\to M$ we have $rj=\mathrm{id}$ and $jr=e_M$. In particular $e_M^2=e_M$, its image is exactly $M^G$, and its restriction to $M^G$ is the identity. These are finite-sum and linearity calculations, valid for arbitrary $M$.

source.place: Tag 0H36 (remark-when-iso): explicit Reynolds argument extending the invertible-order observation to modules.

proof.text: Write $T=B\otimes_A M$ and $U=B\otimes_A M^G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property], the $A$-linear maps $x\mapsto1\otimes j(x)$ and $m\mapsto1\otimes r(m)$ extend uniquely to $B$-linear maps $J:U\to T$ and $R:T\to U$, respectively, with $J(b\otimes x)=b\otimes j(x)$ and $R(b\otimes m)=b\otimes r(m)$. The tensor product in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is generated by pure tensors. Consequently the rule $g(b\otimes m)=b\otimes g(m)$ defines a $B$-linear group action on $T$: the action laws hold on these generators. The image of $d$ in $B$ is a unit, with inverse the image of $u$; apply the calculation of Step 1 over $B$ and call its averaging operator $e_T$. On a pure tensor, $e_T(b\otimes m)=b\otimes e_M(m)$ by tensor bilinearity.

source.place: Tags 00CV (section-tensor-product) and 00CX (lemma-tensor-product): extension of scalars universal property; explicit action and averaging calculation.

proof.text: On $b\otimes x\in U$, $RJ(b\otimes x)=b\otimes rj(x)=b\otimes x$; on $b\otimes m\in T$, $JR(b\otimes m)=b\otimes jr(m)=e_T(b\otimes m)$. Thus $RJ=\mathrm{id}_U$ and $JR=e_T$, by the pure-tensor generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Each $J(b\otimes x)$ is fixed by $G$, so $J$ lands in $T^G$; let $\alpha:U\to T^G$ be its corestriction. For $y\in T^G$, Step 1 over $B$ gives $J(R(y))=e_T(y)=y$. Hence $R|_{T^G}$ and $\alpha$ are mutual inverses. This proves the stated comparison is an isomorphism, using no preservation-of-injections or flatness assertion.

source.place: Tags 0H36 (remark-when-iso) and 0BRH (lemma-base-change-invariants): explicit split-map argument, replacing the flatness-only exact-sequence argument of 0BRH.

proof.text: Let $f:M\to N$ be an equivariant $A$-linear map. It maps $M^G$ into $N^G$, and $f(e_M(m))=u\sum_gf(g(m))=u\sum_gg(f(m))=e_N(f(m))$. The two comparison composites for $f$ both send $b\otimes x$ to $b\otimes f(x)$. For an $A$-algebra map $v:B\to B'$, the induced tensor maps commute with $G$ and the two comparison composites both send $b\otimes x$ to $v(b)\otimes x$. These additive maps agree on all tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. These equalities prove naturality in both variables (and simultaneously for a pair $(v,f)$).

source.place: Tags 00CV (section-tensor-product) and 00CX (lemma-tensor-product): uniqueness on pure tensors and explicit naturality formulas.

proof.text: Now suppose $M=C$ with the stated algebra action. Its fixed elements form an $A$-subalgebra: $g(1)=1$, $g(cc')=g(c)g(c')$, and every $g$ fixes the image of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property], $c\mapsto1\otimes g(c)$ extends to a $B$-algebra map on $B\otimes_A C$; the extension for $g^{-1}$ is its inverse, as their composites fix pure tensors. Thus the action of Step 2 is by $B$-algebra automorphisms, and $D=(B\otimes_A C)^G$ is a $B$-subalgebra. The map $C^G\to D$, $c\mapsto1\otimes c$, is an $A$-algebra homomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property] it extends to a $B$-algebra homomorphism $\beta:B\otimes_A C^G\to D$, $b\otimes c\mapsto b(1\otimes c)=b\otimes c$. Its underlying linear map equals $\alpha$ of Step 3 on every pure tensor and hence everywhere by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; therefore it is bijective. Its inverse preserves products since, if $\beta(a)=y$ and $\beta(a')=y'$, then $\beta(aa')=yy'$; it preserves sums, scalars and the unit by the same uniqueness of preimages. Thus it is the required $B$-algebra isomorphism. Step 4 supplies its naturality as well. No flatness of $B$ or $C$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product): algebra base-change universal property, with the multiplicative and inverse checks written explicitly.

proof_origin.place: Explicit Reynolds and split-tensor argument extending Tag 0H36 (remark-when-iso); Tag 0BRH (lemma-base-change-invariants) only supplies the flat-case comparison for context. Tensor universal properties are cited separately.
